# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

issue_comments.body:
Walkthrough

**Changes: History pagination** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Scheduled-time pagination**
`reports.py`|`history` filters using the scheduled-time cursor and orders by `scheduled_at DESC, id DESC`. When an extra row exists, it returns the scheduled time of the last page row as the next cursor. Otherwise, the next cursor is `None`.|
**Change:** Feature
Merge Risk: Moderate · up to 6cf08

History pagination can silently omit deliveries that share the same scheduled time at a page boundary. Users paging through report history may miss entries. Fix the cursor so it carries both the scheduled time and the ID before merging.
Architecture risk: Low · up to 6cf08

The change affects 1 source area. **Changed areas:** `reports.py`
Review details

**Systems and components** - _observed_ — 1 changed file mapped to reports.py. **Before / after behavior** - _observed_ — Modified behavior in reports.py: `history` replaces the `id < cursor` filter and descending-ID ordering with a scheduled-time cursor filter and ordering by `scheduled_at DESC, id DESC`. It now returns the scheduled time of the last page row as the next cursor when more than `limit` rows are fetched, instead of returning that row’s ID.
Finishing Touches

Generate unit tests (beta)

- [ ] Commit to this branch - [ ] Create a new PR
- [ ] Autofix · Keep fixing CodeRabbit findings and required CI, and resolving merge conflicts

review_comments.body:
**🟠 High · History pages omit deliveries**

When a page boundary splits deliveries with the same scheduled time, `history` stores only the boundary timestamp in `next_cursor`, then filters with `scheduled_at < cursor`; remaining rows at that timestamp are excluded, so callers never see those deliveries.

Include both `scheduled_at` and `id` in the cursor, and filter the next page lexicographically by that pair.

review_comments.body:
**🟡 Medium · History pages slow as records grow**

When the deliveries table grows, sQLite has no index matching the `(scheduled_at, id)` ordering, so each `history` request scans and sorts deliveries; latency and temporary sorting work grow with the table and can exhaust query time or temporary storage.

Add a composite index on `(scheduled_at, id)` to support the history ordering.

review_comments.body:
**🟡 Medium · Existing cursors break after upgrade**

When a page is fetched with one version and its cursor is passed to another version during deployment, the new code interprets a cursor from the previous version as a scheduled timestamp, although that version emitted a delivery ID. Passing that cursor to the new CLI can return an empty or incorrect page, so pagination stops or repeats during a mixed-version rollout.

Version the cursor and preserve support for the previous ID-based cursor during rollout, or explicitly invalidate old cursors and require pagination to restart.

Version the cursor and preserve support for the previous ID-based cursor during rollout, or explicitly invalidate old cursors and require pagination to restart.
~~~

</details>
